what: The lines of the svg placed inside the panel (path·circle·line·polyline·rect) are baked into Lottie, and once ⅔ of the panel’s height from its top edge rises above the bottom of the screen, each line is drawn from start to end with trim (2s, cubic-bezier(.346,.194,.592,1)) — a path holding several branches draws every branch at once, so overlapping line tracks stretch out together. Filled dots (data-kind=pop) pops out from 0 → 1x in 5 frames, fade turns on from transparent, and slide glides in from a spot data-from away (the original spreading rings, six). Each line can be given its own start (data-at), length (data-dur) and curve (data-ease). Color and thickness read the svg’s computed stroke, fill and stroke-width to follow the skin.

options.dur: Duration to draw one line (s), default 2
options.each: Per-line delay (s), default 0 — all lines move together
options.at: The share of the panel height that must be on screen, default .667 (original scInCheck) — .333 is fn-50in, 0 is jquery.inview (even a little in view)
options.when: With event, instead of on screen entry, it redraws from the start every time an fx:play event is received
options.[data-fx-part=art]: svg to draw — viewBox required. Each line element inside takes data-at (start sec) · data-dur (length sec) · data-ease · data-kind (draw|pop|fade|slide) · data-from (slide start offset "dx,dy")·data-trim=seq (branches in sequence)
options.gate: Do not measure until an element matching this css exists in the document (draw after the loader, e.g. html.is-loaded). Once it exists, wake it with a single scroll event

note: The original revealed a hand-drawn image (png) through a thick trim-line matte (track matte) — the image can’t be carried over, so the consumer draws their own lines directly. With reduced motion the svg stays as is (fully drawn). Without Lottie the svg still shows.
